title: GPT-6 Astra Constructs Candidate Lean 4 Counterexample to the 1971 Ibragimov–Iosifescu Conjecture
whyItMatters: Autonomously constructed and Lean-verified a candidate counterexample to a 55-year-old Central Limit Theorem conjecture for stationary φ-mixing sequences—pending expert audit of its AI-written formal statement.
summary: Released on September 5, 2026 by Epoch AI researcher Tom Adamczewski (github.com/tadamcz/phi-mixing-clt), OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra autonomously constructed a candidate counterexample and Lean 4 disproof of the 1971 Ibragimov–Iosifescu conjecture for φ-mixing stochastic processes—which asked whether every strictly stationary, finite-variance, uniformly mixing (φ-mixing) sequence with diverging partial-sum variance must obey a Central Limit Theorem (and by Iosifescu’s stronger version, a weak invariance principle). Astra’s constructed stationary process satisfies finite second moments, φ-mixing, and divergent variance via rare large fluctuations while normalized partial sums concentrate near zero along a subsequence. Lean’s default kernel verified the proof using only standard axioms, though the work is explicitly tracked as an unaudited candidate disproof pending expert verification that the AI-generated formal statement matches classical probability definitions.
technicalHighlights: Autonomously designed a strictly stationary φ-mixing stochastic process where rare large fluctuations maintain divergent variance while normalized partial sums converge to zero in probability along a subsequence.
Verified cleanly by Lean 4’s default kernel using only standard classical axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), with all code and novelty/misformalization audits published openly on GitHub.
Cataloged on Wikipedia and Wolfram MathWorld as a landmark test case of autonomous AI counterexample generation in classical probability theory.
caveats: Tagged Preprint / Active Review because the Lean formalization of the conjecture itself was AI-generated and has not yet received an independent probabilist’s statement-fidelity audit confirming zero subtle definition mismatches.

scoreRationale.foundational: If statement fidelity holds under expert audit, settles a 55-year-old foundational boundary question in dependent Central Limit Theorem theory (Ibragimov 1971 / Iosifescu 1974).
scoreRationale.ripple: Highlights both the promise of autonomous AI counterexample construction in analysis/probability and the urgent need for human statement-fidelity auditing.
scoreRationale.verification: Kernel-verified in Lean 4 with standard axioms, but scored conservatively pending independent probabilist audit of the AI-formalized problem statement.
scoreRationale.velocity: Autonomously generated a delicate stochastic counterexample and complete Lean 4 proof script for a conjecture open since 1971.
